newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia stocks hard hit by NY drop, local factors.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks hard hit by NY drop, local factors.

text.p: Stock markets across Asia fell sharply on Monday, dragged down by Friday's shakeout on Wall Street and continued uneasiness on several local bourses.
In Tokyo, shares dropped sharply, with the benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares down 715.77 points, or 3.65 percent, at 18,888.69, its lowest level since April 30.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index ended the morning session off 216.52 points, or 1.30 percent, at 16,431.02.
"A depressed mood spread in the market, especially in blue chips, due to the sharp fall in New York and the yen's advance," said a broker at one of Japan's "Big Four" securities houses.
The rising yen hurt Japan's export related stocks, particularly electronics stocks.

On Friday the Dow Jones Industrial average shed 156.78 points, or 1.91 percent, to end the week at 8,031.22. The dollar ended in New York at 1.8450/60 marks against 1.8600/05 at Friday's opening there and at 114.75/85 yen compared with 117.22/27.
The spectre of higher U.S. interest rates on speculation that U.S. economic growth may accelerate and force the Federal Reserve to raise rates hit Hong Kong stocks at the opening.
"The main reason for the fall is the sharp decline on Wall Street and the sharp increase in the U.S. long bond yield on Friday," said Percy Au-Young Ping, research director at DBS Securities.
The U.S. Treasury's key 30-year bond lost 1-1/2 points, bringing the yield to 6.64 percent from 6.52 percent Thursday.
Market talk that July U.S. retail sales rose more than an expected 0.5 to 0.6 percent spooked the bond market and contributed to the rise in yields. The figures are due Wednesday.
Elsewhere in Asia, Malaysian stocks forfeited Friday's gains due to heavy foreign selling which left the key index off 25.95 points, or 2.78 percent, at 906.41.
Stocks in the Philippines were equally hard hit, with the stock index closing down 75.39 points, or 2.85 percent, at 2,572.43.
"It was a bloody market. Foreign investors are still cautious on the outcome of the peso's de facto devaluation," said Carl Valentin, a trader at Asia Pacific Capital Equities.

Continuing confusion over the fate of dual listings of Singapore blue chip stocks continued to press the market, leaving the Straits Times Index off 30.05 points, or 1.55 percent, at 1,913.87, near a 31-month low.
Indonesian shares were under pressure from high interest rates, with the composite index down 4.75 points, or 0.70 percent, at 670.68.
Thai stocks firmed after opening lower as investors awaited the outcome of talks in Tokyo on Monday between Thailand and the International Monetary Fund on an aid package.
After being down over three points, the SET composite index was up 0.87 percent, or 0.14 percent, at 637.72.
Profit-taking erased most early gains in South Korean shares, with the composite index ending the morning session up 2.14 points at 762.98.
Taiwan's red-hot electronics stocks also fell victim to heavy profit taking, which dragged the overall market lower. The main index ended down 96.27 points, or 0.96 percent, at 9,897.27.
The sell-off in New York pushed Australia's All Ordinaries Index down 37.3 points, or 1.38 percent, at 2,674.1 and New Zealand's main index down 30.05 points at 2,508.40.
The U.S. currency firmed slightly in early Asia trading on Monday and was quoted around 1.8500 marks and 115.54 yen.
